question.problem:
Find the shortest distance between the origin and the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(4,0,4)$ where $t=-2$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-2) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-1,\,\sqrt{2},\,1⟩ \\ N(-2) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of the point $P(4,0,4)$ is $p=⟨4,\,0,\,4⟩.$

We need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(-2)$ and the principal normal $N(-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =T(-2)\times N(-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-1,\,\sqrt{2},\,1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(\sqrt{2}\,i+2\,j-\sqrt{2}\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{2},-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the shortest distance between our plane and the origin is given by

$$
d=\frac{|(p-0)\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=\frac{|p\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=|p\cdot n|,
$$

since $‖n‖=1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|p\cdot n| \\  & =|⟨4,0,4⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{2},-1⟩| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}|4+0-4| \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
